body:
## What to build

Allow direct SQLite Margin materialization inside a caller-owned transaction, and preserve the supported `in_transaction` argument behavior inherited from dbplyr. Do not start competing nested transactions or take ownership of the caller's transaction.

## Reproduction and observed behavior

Confirmed on unmodified [6a5f611](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/commit/6a5f611d41bd462f3c933edea1dd0b9861d6e892), installed in an isolated library and exercised without testthat. R 4.6.1, dplyr 1.2.1, dbplyr 2.6.0, DBI 1.3.0, RSQLite 3.53.3.

1. Open an in-memory SQLite connection and copy a tibble with character `g = c("a", "b")` and double `v = c(2, 5)`.
2. Build a query using `summarize_with_margins()`, `total = sum(v, na.rm = TRUE)`, `.grouping = rollup(g)`, and `.id = "id"`. Keep the ordinary label and sort defaults.
3. Call `DBI::dbBegin(con)`.
4. Call `compute(query, name = "report", analyze = FALSE)`.
5. Roll back the caller's transaction.

Expected: successful materialization of the three grouping rows, with transaction completion remaining under the caller's control.

Actual: `cannot start a transaction within a transaction`.

A separate fresh case, with no caller transaction, also fails when `in_transaction = TRUE` is supplied to `compute()`. Ordinary dbplyr tables and Margin results outside the dedicated class accept both usage patterns.

The same defect was verified with a second fixture and an independent ordinary SQL result. Sorted typed-label and unsorted `.id` paths both fail. After failure, caller-created uncommitted marker data remains intact and can be rolled back; source data is unchanged, no staging table remains, and a later compute outside the transaction succeeds. The observed bug is false rejection, not evidence that the current failure commits or rolls back the caller's work.

## Contract, diagnosis, and history

[ADR 0031](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/6a5f611d41bd462f3c933edea1dd0b9861d6e892/design/adr/0031-preserve-sqlite-typed-dimensions-under-margin-order.md) retains direct materialization and ordinary backend behavior; it does not exclude caller transactions.

[The dedicated SQLite compute method](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/6a5f611d41bd462f3c933edea1dd0b9861d6e892/R/sqlite-typed-order.R) unconditionally opens `DBI::dbWithTransaction()`. This conflicts with a transaction already opened by the caller. When `in_transaction = TRUE` is forwarded through `...` to the inner ordinary compute, that path attempts another transaction as well. Choose a transaction/savepoint strategy that preserves atomicity and caller ownership; simply removing failure rollback is not an acceptable fix.

Same-dependency public-API comparison shows success before #640 / #650 (`ad851dbefe99cf1cf6987dc5f0716f6a13d3873b`). Before #653 (`d4ea5f09d5698a6a89b68ecfd62ad450a4089bba`), only the sorted dedicated path failed. #653 / #658 extended this regression to ordinary unsorted `.id` results.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A dedicated Margin result can be materialized inside an existing DBI transaction; the caller can subsequently commit or roll it back.
- [ ] Supported `in_transaction` choices behave consistently with ordinary dbplyr at the public compute boundary and never cause accidental nested transaction starts.
- [ ] Preserve atomic materialization on failure, including overwrite/index failures. Do not commit or discard work performed by the caller before the Margin compute began.
- [ ] Exercise transaction-present/absent, sorted typed/unsorted `.id`, success/failure, and a subsequent successful operation. Verify target contents, source preservation, and internal resource cleanup.
- [ ] Preserve declared types, visible columns, Margin order, and lazy construction's query policy; add public-API regression tests and run the required package checks.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately). Schema-qualified naming and downstream projection defects share the method but do not determine this transaction behavior.
